bihar_raw_news.title: Plans afoot to take bullet train project to UP and Bihar , will make it possible to travel between ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Plans afoot to take bullet train project to UP and Bihar, will make it possible to travel between Delhi and Patna in 4.5 hours: Railways Minister ANI | Updated: Aug 31, 2026 21:37 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 31 (ANI): Travel between Delhi and Lucknow will be reduced to two hours and that between the national capital and Patna to 4.5 hours in the proposed bullet train project covering major cities in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar , Railway Minister Ashwani Vaishnaw said on Monday. Speaking during the inauguration of newly converted and electrified broad-gauge rail line on the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich section, Vaishnaw said that the proposed bullet train corridor will include Agra , Kanpur , Lucknow , Varanasi and Patna and connect these sprawling cities to Delhi. He said the proposed project will drastically cut travel time between the national capital and major cities of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar . The minister said under the project, the estimated travel time between Delhi and Agra (200 km) will be 58 minutes . Time to reach Kanpur from Delhi (455 km) will be 1 hour 50 minutes; the route to Lucknow (495 km) will be 2 hours 12 minutes and it will take three hours to reach Prayagraj (750 km) from the national capital. The proposed bullet train will take about 3 hours 33 minutes to reach Varanasi from Delhi (945 km) and 4.5 hours (1,170 km) to reach Patna. "If the project materialises, it will be the next phase bullet train corridor in the country after the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor and the first to connect the National Capital with many cities of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar ," Vaisnaw said. The proposed corridor will not only provide a huge relief to lakhs of daily passengers but is also expected to boost tourism, business and economic activity across the Delhi-UP- Bihar belt, especially in religious tourism hubs like Agra , Prayagraj, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Patna. Currently, the highest design speed in the Indian railway network is around 180 kmph, achieved by semi-high-speed services such as Vande Bharat. Against this, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) Project has a design speed of 350 kmph and an operational speed of 320 kmph. It is one of the most extensive rail infrastructure programmes undertaken in India, and will connect Mumbai and Ahmedabad in about 1 hour 58 minutes. The first high-speed rail service in the country is expected to commence in August 2027 and the first section to be opened will be from Surat to Vapi. Earlier in the day, Vaishnaw said that India will develop another one lakh semiconductor engineers under the second phase of its semiconductor programme, as the government seeks to strengthen the country's talent pool and build a complete semiconductor ecosystem. Speaking after the launch of Semicon 2.0, the minister said the initiative will focus not only on semiconductor manufacturing but also on developing talent, chip design, equipment, materials, advanced packaging and research and development. bihar_raw_news.content: Sone River water pact ends 25-year dispute: Bihar's 8, Jharkhand's 2 among other regions to avail adequate water ANI | Updated: Aug 31, 2026 21:15 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 31 (ANI): With an agreement signed on the sharing of Sone River water in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the national capital, resolving a 25-year-long-awaited water dispute in eastern India, Bihar 's eight districts and Jharkhand 's two key districts, among other regions in these states, will now have access to irrigation and drinking water. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) would ensure the availability of adequate water for drinking and irrigation to a large population across the districts of Bhojpur, Buxar, Rohtas, Kaimur, Aurangabad, Arwal, Gaya, and Patna in Bihar . Moreover, water would become available for irrigation and drinking purposes in the Palamu, Garhwa, and other regions of Jharkhand . As the agreement was signed in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and his Jharkhand counterpart Hemant Soren, Shah said it will provide irrigation water to lakhs of farmers in large rural areas of both the states, along with drinking water for the people. The minister further said that "issues concerning vast geographical areas, farmers, rural regions, and drinking water supplies in both states have been permanently resolved today." The Sone River water dispute was a 25-year-long sharing disagreement between Bihar and Jharkhand over the allocation of Sone River water originating from the 1973 Bansagar Agreement. When Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in 2000, Jharkhand demanded a formal, defined share of that water. The Sone is a perennial river that rises in the Amarkantak hills of Madhya Pradesh and traverses around 784 km across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar before merging with the Ganga at Koilwar near Patna. The river plays a crucial role in Bihar 's irrigation network through the Sone canal system and supports agriculture across several districts in the state's southern and central regions. The distribution of Sone waters has been governed since 1973 by the tripartite Bansagar Accord involving Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and undivided Bihar . Under the agreement, undivided Bihar was allocated 7.75 million-acre-feet (MAF) of water. The issue gained prominence after Jharkhand was created out of Bihar in November 2000, with a portion of the Sone basin falling within the newly formed state. However, the water entitlement originally assigned to " Bihar " under the Bansagar Accord was never formally apportioned between Bihar and Jharkhand . Jharkhand subsequently began seeking a clearly defined share of the allocation soon after its formation. "Today's agreement between Bihar and Jharkhand has resolved a long-awaited water dispute in eastern India. The agreement reached today regarding the sharing of the Sone River's waters is an excellent example of the 'Team Bharat' vision and cooperative federalism championed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi," Shah said after the signing of the MoU. bihar_raw_news.title: Historic pact settles 25-year Son River water dispute between Bihar and Jharkhand
bihar_raw_news.content: National 31 Aug, 2026 Historic pact settles 25-year Son River water dispute between Bihar and Jharkhand Business To Business, New Delhi, 31 August 2026: A 25-year-old dispute between Bihar and Jharkhand over the sharing of Son River waters was resolved on Monday, with the two states signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in the national capital. Under the agreement, Bihar will receive 5.75 million acre-feet (MAF) of water from the river, while Jharkhand has been allocated 2.00 MAF. The MoU was signed in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Bihar Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, along with senior officials from the Centre and both state governments. Describing the agreement as historic, Chief Minister Choudhary expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. He said the long-pending and complex dispute was resolved through the Centre's initiative, continuous dialogue, and effective mediation. According to him, the agreement is not merely a water-sharing arrangement but also marks a new chapter of cooperation, trust, and shared development between Bihar and Jharkhand. The Chief Minister recalled that under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement, out of the total 14.25 MAF water available in the Son River, Madhya Pradesh was allocated 5.25 MAF, Uttar Pradesh 1.25 MAF, and the then undivided Bihar 7.75 MAF. After Jharkhand was created in 2000, a dispute emerged over the division of Bihar's share of 7.75 MAF between the two states. He noted that significant progress on the issue was made during the 27th meeting of the Eastern Zonal Council, chaired by HM Amit Shah in Ranchi on July 10, 2025. The subsequent rounds of technical and administrative discussions eventually led to a final consensus between the two states. The agreement is expected to provide a major boost to irrigation, drinking water supply, and industrial development in the plateau and drought-prone regions of southern Bihar and Jharkhand. Improved water availability is likely to expand irrigation coverage, ease drinking water shortages, and strengthen long-term water security in both states. According to the Chief Minister, the settlement will also accelerate plans for reservoir construction and the proposed Son-Falgu river-linking project, aimed at improving water utilisation. The initiative is expected to enhance water availability in several parts of south Bihar, including Gaya. Adequate flow in the Falgu River would also benefit pilgrims visiting Gaya during the annual Pitrapaksha Mela, facilitating rituals such as tarpan and pind daan. Highlighting the wider significance of the accord, he said the Son River is one of the major southern tributaries of the Ganga and its catchment area plays a crucial role in the agricultural and economic activities of eastern India. Therefore, the agreement carries long-term importance not only for Bihar and Jharkhand but also for water management and regional development across eastern India. Choudhary also thanked the Union Jal Shakti Ministry, the Jharkhand government, and the officials and experts associated with the negotiations.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to Replace 'Fail' with 'Eligible for Skill Development' on Marksheets - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar to Replace ‘Fail’ with ‘Eligible for Skill Development’ on Marksheets 31 Aug 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar Government has decided to replace the word “Fail” with “Eligible for Skill Development” on the marksheets of students who do not clear the Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations from the current academic session. Key Points: State: The initiative has been announced by the Bihar Government which will apply to students appearing for Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations . New Terminology: The word “Fail” will be replaced by “Eligible for Skill Development” on the marksheet. Implementation: The Education Department will amend the existing rules and issue necessary instructions to the Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) . Current Academic Session: The change is proposed to be implemented from the current academic session . Skill-Based Pathway: Students who do not clear the board examination will be able to pursue vocational training programmes through the Bihar Board of Open Schooling and Examination (BBOSE) . Objective: The move aims to reduce the stigma and psychological pressure associated with academic failure . Student Potential: The government emphasised that failure to secure the required marks in an examination does not necessarily reflect a student's talent or future potential . Supplementary Examination: Students appearing for Class 10 supplementary examinations will be provided with special one-month preparation sessions . Remedial Support: The special classes are intended to help students improve their preparation and chances of clearing the examination . Alternative Education: The initiative promotes greater acceptance of vocational and skill-based learning as an alternative educational pathway. Broader Reform: The decision forms part of Bihar’s broader efforts to provide students with opportunities beyond conventional textbook-based education . bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar , Jharkhand settle Son River water dispute after 26 years | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: New Delhi: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren exchange documents of an agreement to resolve the 26-year-old dispute over sharing the waters of the Son River between Bihar and Jharkhand, in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil, in New Delhi on Monday, August 31, 2026. (Photo: IANS/X/@samrat4bjp) India 31st August 2026 Patna, August 31 (IANS) Bihar and Jharkhand have reached a historic agreement on sharing the waters of the Son River, ending a dispute that had dragged on for 26 years. Under the settlement, Bihar will receive 5.57 million acre‑feet (MAF) of water, while Jharkhand will get 2 MAF from the total allocation of 7.75 MAF. The consensus was reached during a meeting in New Delhi chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, attended by Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Paatil. Announcing the development through a post on X, Choudhary described the resolution as a “historic achievement in Bihar’s interest.” He said the agreement would increase water availability for irrigation, benefit farmers, strengthen agriculture and give fresh momentum to development in Bihar. He also noted that Jharkhand would benefit from the arrangement and expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. The dispute dates back to 1973, when an agreement under the Bansagar Project allocated 7.75 MAF of water to undivided Bihar, alongside Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. With Jharkhand carved out of Bihar in 2000, the new state sought a share of the Son River’s water, citing its source and catchment area. Bihar maintained its claim to the full allocation, leading to a prolonged standoff. The disagreement stalled Bihar’s proposed Indrapuri Reservoir Project, as Jharkhand withheld its No Objection Certificate (NOC) amid the dispute. With the new agreement, both states now have defined shares, paving the way for renewed progress on water‑management and irrigation projects. The resolution is seen as significant for Bihar’s agriculture, particularly in areas dependent on Son River irrigation, while Jharkhand gains clarity on its entitlement. The settlement marks a breakthrough in the long‑running water dispute and is expected to strengthen cooperation between the two neighbouring states on resource management.

bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Govt To Launch Shikshak Samadhan Portal On September 5, Teachers Issues to be Resolved in 30 Days By Faham Ehraj Last Updated: Aug 31, 2026, 16:57 IST Bihar will launch the Shikshak Samadhan Portal on September 5, 2026. Teacher’s issues will be resolved within 30 days. Read the article below to get complete details. Bihar Govt To Launch Shikshak Samadhan Portal On September 5 Register for Result Updates The Bihar government is all set to launch the Shikshak Samadhan Portal on September 5, 2026. The day is celebrated as Teachers Day in India. The Shikshak Samadhan Portal will be launched in Patna. The main aim of this portal is to resolve teachers' issues within 30 days. Bihar education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari shared this update through the official X handle of the education department. The state government believes that a teacher cannot fully focus on the job if he or she is facing issues in life. The government plans to resolve these problems for the teachers. The portal is part of a larger reform plan for the education department. Read the article below to get more details. Shikshak Samadhan Portal to Resolve teachers Issues within 30 Days The state government has set a clear target for the Shikshak Samadhan Portal. Every teacher's issues must be resolved within 30 days. If the target is not met then the officials will be answerable. They may also undergo an investigation. Tiwari spoke at the Seemanchal Conclave in Purnia on Saturday. He said that the government plans to resolve the issues and problems of the teachers. This will help teachers give their full attention to their work. The minister also said that the state government is aiming to give solutions to teachers' issues within 30 days. State Honours for Teachers and Education Reform in Bihar On the occasion of Teachers Day educators from every district will receive state honours. The preparations for this event are going on. The same day will also see the launch of the Shikshak Samadhan Portal. Tiwari said that the government has decided to perform through reform. He added that the education department will see so much reform that the state of Bihar performs automatically. A review meeting of Bihar Education Department was held at the District Guest House in Purna on August 29. The meeting discussed the progress and quality of the education system in the district. Various issues related to schools were also covered in detail. Tiwari said that a strong education system is the solid foundation of a developing Bihar. The Shikshak Samadhan Portal is a big step in this direction. It will bring relief to thousands of teachers across the state. Teachers across Bihar are hopeful that this portal will solve their problems quickly. The Shikshak Samadhan Portal will work as a single platform for all teacher complaints. Teachers can use this portal to register their issues without any delay.

bihar_raw_news.title: Mumbai: 4 Minors From Bihar , Haryana Rescued In Santacruz, Reunited With Families
bihar_raw_news.content: Mumbai, August 31, 2026: The Vakola police recently rescued four minors who had arrived in Mumbai from Bihar and Haryana to see the city and reunited them with their respective families. Rescue Operation The incident came to light on August 13 when the Vakola police received information around 1.30 am that four minors were roaming outside Santacruz railway station on the eastern side, while some unidentified persons were allegedly attempting to take them away. #WATCH | #Mumbai : 4 Minors From Bihar, Haryana Rescued In Santacruz, Reunited With Families Reported by @meghakuchik1 #MumbaiNews #Bihar pic.twitter.com/1lz0V144jl — Free Press Journal (@fpjindia) August 31, 2026 The police immediately dispatched a Nirbhaya Pathak to the spot. Police Sub-Inspector Snehal Kesare and constable Sunil Gaikwad, along with the Nirbhaya Pathak team, reached Prabhat Colony Road near Jaku Club in Santacruz East. The police found the minors frightened and hungry and brought them to the Vakola police station. They were provided food, given medical examinations and subsequently questioned as part of the inquiry. Of the four minors, three were siblings, two girls and a boy, from Danapur, Patna, in Bihar, while the fourth, a boy, was from Pabnera village, Sonipat, in Haryana. They were identified as Hussain Satana, 14, Jainab Satana, 15, and Masija Sutana, 3, all residents of Danapur, and Navin Chandar, 12, from Sonipat, Haryana. The Vakola police formed teams and assigned different tasks to the officers and personnel. Under the guidance of Navnath Ghuge, Senior Police Inspector, Vakola police station, Crime Police Inspector Vaibhav Swami, Assistant Police Inspector Sukenishi Karande, Police Sub-Inspector Snehal Kesare, and police constables Vrushali Rajpure, Sunil Gaikwad, Tejashree Thokale and Raut were involved in the investigation. Police Trace Families The police carried out social media monitoring and used search engines to check all-India databases for any cases involving the minors, including kidnapping, missing-person reports, murder or other offences registered at police stations across the country. During the inquiry, the police learned that the minors had come to Mumbai for the first time as they wanted to see the city. They had not informed their parents or relatives about their plan to travel to Mumbai. According to the police, the three siblings had gone to a fair in their village in Danapur, Bihar. The fair was being held for several days, and the children were staying there. They later boarded a train and travelled to Mumbai without informing their parents. Chandar, who was travelling on the same train, also accompanied them to Mumbai. Police Sub-Inspector Kesare said the children were very young and could not say the name of the train or provide details about the route they had taken. They only told the police that they wanted to see Mumbai. Children Reunited The siblings' parents work odd jobs in Bihar, and the family has several other children. bihar_raw_news.title: MSCI rebalancing to test new closing auction system ; stocks may see flows - IANS LIVE
bihar_raw_news.content: MSCI rebalancing to test new closing auction system; stocks may see flows IANS August 31, 2026 10:38 AM Share on | Mumbai, Aug 31 (IANS) The MSCI index rebalancing on Monday is set to provide the first major test of the new closing auction session (CAS) with passive funds expected to execute large trades in final minutes of the trading session. The rebalancing will take place towards the close of trading -- with four stocks, including Adani Energy Solutions, set to be included in the MSCI Standard Index. These stocks are expected to see potential inflows, other stocks that are being excluded from the index could witness outflows. As per market estimates, Adani Energy Solutions and the other three stocks could see inflows of around $280 million to $400 million, while the three exclusions could face outflows of $110 million to $150 million, according to market estimates. However, experts are closely watching the impact of the rebalancing on the new CAS mechanism that was introduced earlier in August. Under the new system, a single equilibrium price discovered at 3:30 pm becomes the official closing price. Since trading in the futures and options segment ends at 3:15 pm, with order placement resuming from 3:20 pm to 3:30 pm, passive funds will have a narrow window to execute their rebalancing trades. The market experts have expected that stocks outside the F&O segment to see the rebalancing proceed broadly as in the past. However, stocks in the F&O segment could witness increased volatility as funds seek to execute trades without creating tracking errors. In addition, concerns have also emerged over liquidity and participation during the CAS which could make it difficult to fully match large institutional orders. Moreover, insufficient liquidity after 3:15 pm could force passive funds to defer some trades to the next session, potentially resulting in tracking errors. The MSCI exercise will therefore offer a closely watched test of whether the new closing mechanism can efficiently absorb large, benchmark driven flows without causing significant price distortions. --IANS ag/

bihar_raw_news.title: BPSC postpones online application process for over 32000 Bihar teacher jobs
bihar_raw_news.content: ANI The BPSC has deferred the start of TRE 4.0 registration, which was earlier scheduled for September 1. The recruitment covers 32,388 teacher vacancies across Bihar’s government schools. Patna: The Bihar Public Service Commission on Monday postponed the commencement of the online application process for the fourth phase of the Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE-4), citing procedural changes. The online application process for recruitment to 32,388 vacant school teacher posts under the Bihar Education Department was scheduled to begin from September 1. A release issued by the BPSC said procedural changes led to the postponement, and that a fresh date would be announced soon. The Commission had on August 18 issued a notification asking aspirants to submit online applications for the teaching posts from September 1, hours after students, demonstrating at Patna's Gardani Bagh area, threatened to gherao the education minister if the exam schedule was not announced "within 24 hours". Opposition leaders in Bihar like RJD's Tejashwi Yadav and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya had also come out in support of the protesting students. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Choudhary in Delhi for key meetings with HM Shah, Jal Shakti Minister Patil
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Choudhary in Delhi for key meetings with HM Shah, Jal Shakti Minister Patil By: IANS On: Monday, August 31, 2026 11:54 AM Google News Follow Us Patna, Aug 31 (IANS) Bihar Chief Minister, Samrat Choudhary, is in Delhi on Monday for a series of meetings with senior Union ministers, in a visit that is being closely watched for both political and administrative reasons. The visit comes after he assumed office and at a time when the Bihar government is dealing with several pressing challenges, including development, floods, law and order, water resources and infrastructure. A high-level meeting between Choudhary and Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to take place at Janpath. Although the official agenda has not been disclosed, the meeting is expected to cover several issues concerning Bihar, including law and order, development programmes, administrative requirements and Centre-State coordination. Law and order is likely to be an important component of the discussions, given its political sensitivity in Bihar. The Chief Minister may also brief the Union Home Minister on the state government’s priorities for strengthening the security apparatus and improving crime control. Choudhary may also seek greater coordination and central support for major projects involving roads, transport, urban development and other infrastructure initiatives. Faster approvals and implementation of centrally supported schemes could be among the state’s priorities. Another significant engagement during the Delhi visit is Choudhary’s meeting with Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil. The meeting assumes particular importance for Bihar, where large parts of the state face recurring floods every year. Rising water levels in rivers originating in Nepal, as well as the Ganga, Gandak, Kosi and other major rivers, frequently affect several districts. Against this backdrop, flood control, irrigation and long-term water management are expected to be key issues during the meeting. The Bihar government is likely to seek central assistance for strengthening embankments, improving flood protection systems, managing rivers and expanding irrigation infrastructure. Issues concerning drinking water and the effective utilisation of water resources may also come up for discussion. The timing of the meeting is significant as Bihar continues to seek long-term solutions to its recurring flood problem rather than relying primarily on annual relief and rescue operations. The state could use the meeting to place proposals for permanent flood-control measures and improved river management before the Centre. Choudhary’s Delhi visit, therefore, comes against the backdrop of challenges on multiple fronts. While the government is seeking to accelerate development projects, it must simultaneously address floods, law and order and infrastructure-related concerns. –IANS ajk/rad (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo source: IANS) India 31st August 2026 West Champaran, August 31 (IANS) Floodwaters entered several low-lying areas of Bihar's West Champaran district after around 180,000 cusecs of water was released from the Valmiki Nagar Gandak Barrage following the devastating floods in neighbouring Nepal. Residents of Chakdahwa and nearby villages reported severe difficulties in travelling through the flooded areas, with people having to commute through water for nearly three kilometres. Locals also highlighted poor road conditions, lack of electricity and prolonged infrastructure-related problems that have continued to affect the region. Following the release of around 164,000 cusecs of water from the Gandak Barrage, the main road connecting Chakdaha, Jhautala and Bintoli in Bagaha-2 has been submerged under nearly five feet of water. Around 3,000 people depend on this route and the surrounding facilities for their daily needs, including access to medical treatment. Residents said that the flooding has made even essential travel extremely difficult during the rainy season. Anju Kumari, a resident of the area, said she had travelled to Bhedihari for a doctor's appointment for her one-year-old child and was returning to her village, Chakdahwa. Describing the difficulties faced by residents every monsoon, she said, "We have to walk through water throughout the entire rainy season. It is a huge problem, but what can we do?" She appealed to the government to take steps to improve connectivity in the area. "The government should build a road," she said. Suraj Kumar, a resident of Chak Dawa, also described the situation as extremely difficult for villagers who have to travel through the flooded route. "The situation is very bad. It is a three-kilometre journey to the city. The road is good, but there are many problems. We walk through water up to our necks," he said. Another resident, Haslim Gaddi, said that the problem has persisted for years, with villagers continuing to struggle due to inadequate roads and the absence of proper lighting. "The situation is very bad. We travel three kilometres through water. Neither is the road good, nor is there any lighting. No one pays heed to our problems. We have been facing this problem for years," Gaddi said. Sohail Ansari said that residents are forced to cross deep water during the rainy season, while also facing the additional danger posed by wildlife because the area falls within the Valmiki Tiger Reserve. "The situation is very bad. We have to cross the water. We have to travel through six feet of water for three months. Being part of the Valmiki Tiger Reserve, there is also a constant fear of animals," Ansari said. Meanwhile, as a precautionary measure, the district administration has already shifted more than 5,000 people living in vulnerable and low-lying areas to safer locations. The flood situation is also being closely monitored in other vulnerable districts of Bihar, where authorities have made necessary arrangements to deal with any emergency arising from rising water levels. The Bihar government has appealed to residents to remain alert and follow official instructions.

national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu today said that the textile and apparel sector is not only an important part of India’s cultural heritage but also provides livelihood to millions of people. Addressing the convocation ceremony of the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), the President called upon students to adopt a global outlook while remaining rooted in the country’s rich cultural heritage and values. Emphasising the growing role of women in the fashion industry, the President said around 85% of the nearly 4000 students present at the event are women. She said India has immense potential to expand its global presence in fashion and textile technology. The President urged students to use their knowledge, skills and creativity to connect the country’s traditional textile heritage with contemporary markets and new technologies. Calling upon the youth to contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the President said students should not remain merely job seekers but should strive to become job providers and create employment opportunities for others. President Murmu said that over the past four decades, NIFT students and professionals have made significant achievements at the national and international levels, bringing recognition to India. She appreciated the contribution of NIFT professionals in promoting Indian textiles, silk and design traditions on the global stage. President Murmu congratulated the graduating students, their parents and award winners for outstanding academic performance. Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh said, in 2008, then President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam delivered the NIFT convocation address, and after 18 years, again President Droupadi Murmu blessed the students. He said around four thousand students today received their degrees. Textiles Secretary and Chairperson of the Board of Governors, NIFT, Neelam Shami Rao said the students are graduating at an exciting time for textiles, fashion and design. She said the industry they will enter is changing at a remarkable pace, and the boundaries between craft, fashion, design, engineering, creativity, technology and textiles are becoming increasingly fluid. The Secretary said the fashion of tomorrow can draw strengths from the craft traditions of India.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 51 Government notifies Semicon 2.0 scheme with 1.27 lakh crore rupees outlay
national_raw_news.content: The government today notified the Semicon 2.0 scheme with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore to boost the chip manufacturing ecosystem in the country. With this, India could account for nearly 10 percent of the global semiconductor industry market in the coming years and is expected to play a much bigger role in the global semiconductor value chain, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said while addressing a press briefing in New Delhi today. Mr. Vaishnaw added that the focus of the Government is towards making the country firmly embedded in the global semiconductor value chain, from wafer fabrication to chip production. After releasing the notifications for all six pillars of the Semicon India Programme 2.0., Mr Vaishnaw noted that there is confidence among global semiconductor industry stakeholders that India is the right destination for major investments in the coming decades. The Minister underlined that the speed at which projects have moved from approval to ground-breaking and then to commercial production in Semicon 1.0, has been particularly noted by the industry. Further, Mr. Vaishnaw said India’s talent pool, policy certainty and ease of working have contributed to the industry’s growing interest in making India a base for semiconductor manufacturing and design. He added the country’s objective is to become an indispensable part of the global semiconductor supply chain, with global industries increasingly depending on India for production and design. Mr Vaishnaw emphasised that developing the entire ecosystem in the country will be foundational for sustained growth of India’s semiconductor industry over the next 50 years.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 201 Death toll in Nepal flash flood rises to 903, while more than 4,247 people still missing
national_raw_news.content: In Nepal, the death toll from last week’s devastating floods and mudslides has risen to 903, while more than 4,247 people remain untraceable. According to the Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, the figure has increased from Sunday’s figure of 2,502. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts of Nepal as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded. Meanwhile, at least 933 workers are believed to be trapped at around half a dozen hydropower projects. Rescue teams backed by India and other experts are searching around half a dozen blocked hydropower tunnels, including Trishuli-3A. In Tibet, the death toll currently stands at 16, with 546 reported to be missing. The disaster sent a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris through towns and villages along the Nepal-Tibet border. An Indian tunnel rescue team is working with the Nepali Army at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Earth-moving machinery and soldiers have been working through the night to clear debris. Nepali Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said the massive deposits are making tunnel access difficult. A preliminary study by Nepali scientists found the floods were triggered by a massive ice-rock avalanche at around 5,200 metres in Rasuwa’s Langtang-Lirung area. The debris entered the Lhende River before surging through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli. Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah called the floods an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster”, with nearly 21,000 security personnel involved in rescue operations. The Red Cross estimates more than 90,000 people were affected, while authorities continue recovering and identifying bodies.

national_raw_news.title: 8 hours ago | International 334 PM Modi arrives in Bishkek on two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan; to attend SCO Summit and meet several ...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Bishkek on a two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. He was received at the airport by Kasymaliev Adylbek Aleshovich, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. A traditional Kyrgyz dance performance was also organised to welcome him. Mr Modi is visiting Kyrgyzstan at the invitation of President Sadyr Zhaparov for 26th SCO Summit. On the first day of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. He will also participate in several other programmes. Mr Modi will address the SCO Summit tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will first interact with the Friends of India in Bishkek today. He will then visit the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Park and pay floral tributes at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. The statue was unveiled by Mr Modi during his visit to Kyrgyzstan in the year 2015. The Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings with several leaders of SCO member countries today. These include meetings with the Presidents of Armenia, Kyrgyzstan and Iran, as well as a bilateral meeting with the President of Russia. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games today. The event celebrates the rich and vibrant cultural heritage of Central Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation tomorrow, the first of September. Vikalp Shukla, Akashvani News, Bishkek.” In his departure statement on Saturday, Mr Modi said he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, based on “security, connectivity and opportunity”. He also said India will work with SCO members towards a region free from “terrorism, separatism and extremism”. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. He said the visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen its civilisational connect with the region and advance the shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity. The summit theme is “25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity. The summit’s priorities include counter-terrorism, regional stability and coordination on cross-border threats. The Bishkek Declaration and other summit texts are expected to be finalised during heads-of-state session tomorrow.

national_raw_news.title: Gujarat to host 11th Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit in January next year 2 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The 11th Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit 2027 will take place from 10th to 12th January next year in Gandhinagar. The theme of this summit is Viksit Gujrat – Shaping Global future. Addressing a curtain-raiser press conference in New Delhi today, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendrabhai Patel said it is Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision that Gujarat should not merely be seen as an investment destination but should emerge as a growth engine for the country. He said the State government has realised this vision on the ground and is working to make Gujarat the soft power of the country. Mr Patel added that the government is promoting green hydrogen and green energy and has introduced sector-specific, holistic policies to promote ease of doing business. Referring to the ‘Saptdhara’, or seven streams of development, announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the ramparts of the Red Fort during his Independence Day speech, Mr. Patel said it covers key sectors including agriculture, food processing, technology and innovation. He said these sectors will receive further impetus through the Vibrant Gujarat Summit. On the occasion, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said that Gujarat has transformed itself in line with future requirements and has emerged as one of the country’s leading investment destinations. He said Gujarat has developed a strong investment ecosystem, supported by close linkages between entrepreneurs and investors. Dr. Mandaviya said, Gujarat offers opportunities across various sectors and described the semiconductor industry as a sunrise sector with significant growth potential. The Vibrant Gujarat summit has evolved as one of the most reputed global forums for business networking, knowledge sharing and strategic partnerships for inclusive growth and sustainable development. The Vibrant Gujarat initiative was conceptualised in 2003 under the leadership of Narendra Modi, then Chief Minister of Gujarat. Over the years, the summit has expanded from an investment-focused event into a broad platform connecting governments, multinational corporations, investors, entrepreneurs, policymakers, academics and innovators. The Vibrant Gujarat model is designed to connect overseas governments and companies with Gujarat’s industrial ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: BJP State Working Committee meeting enters second day in Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: The second day of the BJP State Working Committee meeting is being held today in Orchha, Madhya Pradesh. During the meeting, Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav visited the Ram Raja Temple this morning and offered prayers. After the visit, the Chief Minister reviewed the development work going on at Ram Raja Lok. He spoke about preserving the historical buildings and promoting Orchha’s traditional style of architecture. On the second day of the meeting, a special workshop is being held under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The workshop will finalise the upcoming programmes related to public service, good governance and strengthening the party organisation. Several senior BJP leaders attended the first day of the meeting. State BJP President Hemant Khandelwal said that service, values and the welfare of the last person are the foundation of the BJP’s ideology. State in-charge Dr. Mahendra Singh stressed the need to strengthen the organisation at the booth level to achieve the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan spoke about taking farmer welfare schemes to the people. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia linked the growing use of UPI, startups and technology with new opportunities for young people. Deputy Chief Minister Rajendra Shukla said that the Ken-Betwa project is important for the development of the Bundelkhand region. The meeting also discussed issues related to women’s empowerment, tribal communities and employment.
